items.title: Associated primes of a module with a prime-cyclic filtration lie among the primes of the filtration
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Given a filtration of M whose successive quotients are of the form R modulo a prime, the lemma states that every associated prime of M occurs among the primes attached to the filtration (statement lines 15369-15379). The proof does not invoke the theory of primary decomposition, which is not yet available at that point: it inducts on the length of the filtration, and in the critical case where the witness element does not already lie in the penultimate submodule it multiplies the witness by an element of the last prime outside the associated prime, an operation that preserves the annihilator while pushing the element one step down the filtration (proof lines 15381-15390). That pushing-down trick is the content of the argument. H2.
